# Jiva

> Jiva is a free macOS meeting recorder that runs entirely on your Mac and remembers who said what, across every meeting. Recording, transcription, speaker recognition, summaries and search all run on-device: no cloud, no account, and no bot joins the call. Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (macOS 14.4+).

## What Jiva does

- **Records both sides of a call** on your Mac (Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Webex, Slack huddles). No bot joins the meeting.
- **Live, on-device transcription** that works offline.
- **Speaker memory**: recognizes the same voice across meetings, so transcripts show real names instead of "Speaker 1".
- **Live summary overlay** beside the call, with a suggested response and Assist / Recap.
- **Ask any past meeting**: answers are cited to the exact moment they were said.
- **Action items**: pulled out automatically, each linked to where it was said.
- **Screens shown in the meeting**: shared slides and documents are captured inline in the transcript (optional, off by default).
- **To-dos**: one list of what you owe and what others owe you, typed or dictated; each card shows the next step, and opens to why it matters and a draft reply.
- **Hold-to-talk dictation**: hold Right Command, speak in any app, and Jiva types it.
- **Calendar (optional)**: read-only Google Calendar access for a reminder before each meeting and one-click Join & Record.
- **Claude and other AI apps (optional)**: a local MCP server lets Claude search your meetings. Only the passages that app reads leave your Mac.
- **Second brain with Claude (optional)**: turn it on in Settings and the Claude desktop app keeps a store of your people, decisions, work and to-dos from Slack, email, Notion and your meetings, checking hourly on weekdays. It adds to-dos with context, closes them when done, and fixes name spellings in future transcripts. The store stays on your Mac; what Claude reads goes through your own Claude account.
- **Dark mode**: follows your Mac, or pick Light or Dark.

## How it compares

Measured on a public four-person meeting (AMI ES2004a), scored against the human transcript: Jiva gave 90% of words to the right person (a popular AI notetaker: 43%) with 21% of words wrong (that notetaker: 17%). Details: https://jiva.works/benchmarks


Jiva is a local alternative to cloud AI meeting notetakers. The difference: audio and transcripts stay on your Mac, it is free with no account, and it keeps a cross-meeting memory of who said what with citations back to the source.

## Install

- One command: `curl -fsSL https://jiva.works/install.sh | bash` (downloads, verifies the checksum, installs to Applications and opens Jiva)
- Homebrew: `brew install --cask venugopalarjun/jiva/jiva`
- Or download the .dmg: https://github.com/venugopalarjun/jiva/releases/latest/download/Jiva.dmg
- The Welcome window then downloads the on-device models (about 6 GB: Parakeet speech, speaker separation, Whisper refine, Qwen3-4B summaries).

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS 14.4+ on Apple silicon; Android keyboard (beta) for dictation
- Price: free
- Privacy: fully local. Optional integrations (Google Calendar, Claude, the second brain) are off until you turn them on.
- Latest version: 0.1.17 (2026-10-25): One list of what you owe and what you're waiting on. Full history: https://jiva.works/changelog
- Site: https://jiva.works/
- Privacy policy: https://jiva.works/privacy
